defect_summary: The source calls integral f times conjugate(g) an inner product on the pointwise space of complex-valued Riemann-integrable functions and calls the induced quantity an L2 norm. Positive definiteness fails on that space: a nonzero function supported at one point is Riemann integrable but has integral of its squared modulus equal to zero. The pairing is positive semidefinite and the induced quantity is only a seminorm until functions equal almost everywhere are identified; on that quotient they become a genuine inner product and norm.
